# R5.12 — Atomic whole-vector Account cap admission

## Summary

Implements the whole-vector `reserve` admission of the budget owner
(decomposition row 28 — the sibling operation to R5.13's physical-use
fold): `Account::reserve` now checks **every bounded key on every
ancestor** — primary or derived — against the projected level
`consumed + reserved + slice_held + request`, through the owning
`level`/`key_total` fold (PADR-R5-2 B.1 item 3). `tokens.input.total` /
`tokens.output.total` ceilings now actually bind — the baseline checked
only request-named primary keys. Refusing any dimension holds nothing;
the exact boundary admits. Contract: `docs/tickets/181_R5.12__reserve.md`.

**Requirement ids:** REQ-E-207, REQ-D-006 (contributing only — primary
owner of both is R5.19 AC-3; never duplicate ownership).

## What changed

- `crates/hh-budget/src/account.rs` — `reserve` (+35/−23): per-ancestor
  scan over every non-gauge hard key, projected
  `level + quantity.key_total(key) > hard` ⇒ `InsufficientBudget`
  (leaf→root, canonical key order); gauge dims still
  `DimensionNotBudgetable`; refused row ledgered, nothing held.
- `crates/hh-budget/tests/r5_12.rs` (new) — 7-leg AC-1/AC-2 battery on
  scratch `Store::open_test` runs.
- `docs/adr/ADR-0391-…` — 6 owned landing decisions; BL-47 sources +
  regenerated index/triggers.
- `docs/build/runs/R5.12.md` — run ledger (gate verbatim, gap table,
  evidence log/report, split-trigger record + ruling).

## Design decisions (ADR-0391)

Every bounded key projected at every ancestor (not only request-named
primaries); projection reuses `BudgetTree::level` +
`ResourceVector::key_total` — no parallel total fold and no stored
derived amounts; `>` keeps exact-boundary admission while an untouched
key refuses only when already over; gauge hard keys skipped exactly as
`BudgetTree::check` skips them (E5); `requested`/`available` name the
failed bound — a derived refusal reports the request's `key_total`
component sum, never a component.

## Deviations

**645 changed source/test lines vs ≤600 split trigger — recorded
Deviation, accepted under the scoped split ruling (AMEND, commit
